info.name: rSTAR HRMS API
info.description:
HRMS backend API, grouped into folders.

Health   - liveness and readiness, no auth
Auth     - login, OTP, refresh, password reset
Admin    - Organization and Locations (permission-guarded)

ORDER MATTERS the first time through: run Auth top to bottom to capture the token, then Admin > Organization before Admin > Locations, because the location requests read the {{organizationId}} that `create organization` stores.

No bearer token is ever pasted. verify-otp stores it in {{accessToken}} and every request inherits the collection-level Bearer auth that reads it.

Set {{baseUrl}} in the Variables tab, or pick an environment, and go.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Login is two steps: the password is checked first, then a one-time code.

Run these top to bottom once per session. `verify-otp` captures {{accessToken}} and {{refreshToken}}, and every other folder inherits the collection Bearer auth that reads them - nothing is ever pasted.

logout (7) is followed by two requests that are SUPPOSED to return 401: they send the access token and the refresh token it just revoked. That is the whole claim being tested - both halves of the pair die together, so a logged-out client cannot refresh its way back in. 10 and 11 then sign in again, because the folders below need a live token.

forgot-password / reset-password really do change a password. They are last for that reason.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Organisation setup and, as they are built, roles, groups and user access. Everything in here is permission-guarded and today only Super Admin and HR Admin hold any of it.

A 403 names the exact code it wanted in `details.requiredPermission` - grant that rather than guessing at a role.

item.name: Employees
item.description:
Onboarding and the employee record: create, read, update, exit, delete.

Run top to bottom. Request 1 stores {{employeeDetailId}} and everything after it works on that person, ending with a delete - so a full run leaves the database as it found it.

UNLIKE the Admin folder, every permission here is SCOPED. Holding employees.view at OWN returns your own record and nothing else; at TEAM, you and your direct reports; at ALL, the company. A write to a row outside your scope answers 404 rather than 403, because a 403 would confirm that an employee with that id exists.

Exiting somebody is its own endpoint and its own permission (employees.deactivate), not a flag on update. It demands a leaving date and an exit status, and refuses while the person still has direct reports - see requests 7 to 10.
